subject: Struggling to manipulate my results to predict yearlySiteCovs

messages.author: b063227c9709ab9e
messages.subject: Struggling to manipulate my results to predict yearlySiteCovs
parts:
Hi there,

I am running multi-season occupancy models for single-species. I have 31 camera trap sites which were sampled for 12 occasions (60 days truncated into 12 5-day periods) across four seasons. I have various site covariates (e.g. distance to water, vegetation, elevation and whether the camera was placed on a road (yes) or not (no)) and I have various yearly-site-covariates (e.g. rainfall, lion relative abundance, leopard relative abundance). 

I have been through all the modelling steps and arrived at the following best fit model:


bbjdata <- read.csv(file= "bbj_allsurveys_no_comma.csv", header=TRUE)

y <- bbjdata[,2:49]
S <- nrow(bbjdata)
J <- 12
T <- 4

#site level covariates
site.cov <- data.frame(vegetation=bbjdata[,50], elevation=bbjdata[,51], slope=bbjdata[,52], road=bbjdata[,53], water=bbjdata[,54])

#site level covariates
rainfall <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,59:62])
lion <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,63:66])
leopard <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,67:70])
hyaena <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,71:74])
mpred <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,75:78])
spred <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,79:82])
lprey <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,83:86])
mprey <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,87:90])
sprey <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,91:94])
human <- as.matrix(bbjdata[,95:98])

yearly.covs <- data.frame(rainfall, lion, leopard, hyaena, mpred, spred, lprey, mprey, sprey,  human)

#set specialised dataframe
bbjUMF <- unmarkedMultFrame (y=y, siteCovs=site.cov, numPrimary=4, yearlySiteCovs=yearly.covs)
ge.water_lion <- colext(psiformula = ~water, gammaformula = ~ lion, epsilonformula = ~ lion, pformula = ~ road+leopard+lion, data=bbjUMF)

#best fit model
ge.water_lion <- colext(psiformula = ~water, gammaformula = ~ lion, epsilonformula = ~ lion, pformula = ~ road+leopard+lion, data=bbjUMF)

I am able to manipulate, predict and plot the occupancy for distance to water with no problems:

ndwater <- data.frame(water=seq(0, 2800, 400))
predict.psi <- predict(ge.water_lion, type="psi", newdata=ndwater, appendData=TRUE)

my_y <- expression(paste("Occupancy probability (",psi,")"))

plot1 <- ggplot(predict.psi, aes(x=water, y=Predicted))+ geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=Predicted-SE, ymax=Predicted+SE),
        alpha=0.2) + geom_line(size=1) + theme_classic() + labs(y=my_y, x="Distance to water (m)") + 
        scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,0.2)) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,2800)) +
        theme(text=element_text(family = "serif",), axis.text.x = element_text(colour="black", size = 10), 
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black", size = 10)) + theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 12))

plot1

#best fit model
ge.water_lion <- colext(psiformula = ~water, gammaformula = ~ lion, epsilonformula = ~ lion, pformula = ~ road+leopard+lion, data=bbjUMF)

I have tried multiple lines of code to try and predict and plot the effects of my yearlySiteCovs on both colonization and extinction and then the combination of covariates for detection - but I am seriously struggling.


Hope this all makes sense.

Any advice and guidance will be appreciated,

Kind regards,
Jess

messages.author: e6ea535446304d42
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Struggling to manipulate my results to predict yearlySiteCovs
parts:
Hello Jess,

I'm fairly new to this but have had some recent experience.

Firstly, colext models the initial Psi 'state' and then the transitions between each season. With 4 seasons this means you have three transitions S1-S2, S2-S3, S3-S4. The yearly covariates therefore only require three values (one for each transition) but the data input requires four values, so often a dummy value is supplied (NA seems fine??). There are a few posts in this forum about this already by people who actually know what they are talking about, so please refer to them. Your lion data has four values, so the fourth will be ignored (or you can enter in the 4th as NA's).

Your predict values for Psi look good, but your plot uses a ribbon based on predict +/- SE. This is incorrect as you should transform the values into logit space before adding/subtracting SE or CI to a mean, then backtransforming the values. Better yet, use the predicted "lower" and "upper" values which should be the default 95% confidence limits.

Predicting gamma and epsilon requires a value for each of the transitions - in this case three. It should be fairly straight forward for a linear value - just ensure they are of type "numeric" (rather than factor or character).

for starters, try:
ndlion <- data.frame(lion=c(0.12,0.12,0.12))
predict.col<- predict(ge.water_lion, type="col", newdata=ndlion, appendData=TRUE)  

If this works then you should be able to make a 'ndlion' dataframe exploring the different combinations of lion values you have or expect to have and plot the different scenarios.

I hope this works, I hope this is correct and I hope it has helped.

Cheers,
Al
